title: Large-leaved Lime: Ancient Summer Lindens You Can Visit
meta_description: The village lime of central Europe. Schenklengsfeld's, 17.91 metres round, has the largest trunk circumference of any tree in Germany.
intro: A lime has marked the exact spot where three Brussels communes meet since at least 1777, and that is the sort of job this species keeps getting: boundary post, landmark, court, dance floor, the tree a place organises itself around. Schenklengsfeld held its court under its lime from 1557 to 1796; at 17.91 metres round it has the largest trunk circumference of any tree in Germany, and in the 2018 heatwave the village fire brigade pumped 100,000 litres of water onto it. Heede's is widely reported as the thickest lime in Europe and sits on the village coat of arms. Prague has one a president refused to lose, Tomas Garrigue Masaryk having had a castle terrace built around it. Telling a large-leaved lime from a small-leaved one is harder than it sounds, and under Nuremberg's 400 year old tree the sign and the botanists still disagree.
